page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested servers under stress-ng. Multi-core CPU execution, Passmark CPU scores, and Geekbench multi-core workloads fall within the average range. However, a notable hardware tradeoff is observed in memory subsystem performance; while cached small-block reads are average, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is weak, and large-block memory write bandwidth is poor.

Given the dedicated compute resources and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is structured for compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or high-speed local disk I/O. Appropriate workloads include web serving, software compilation, and light text or image processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC architecture offers stable compute capacity for steady-state processing, though workloads requiring heavy, uncached memory operations may experience bottlenecks.
